newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov sees chance of NYC tax surcharge extension.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov sees chance of NYC tax surcharge extension.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki on Tuesday told reporters that there was a chance that the New York City personal income tax surcharge, which expires at year-end, could be extended.
Legislative leaders cautioned that while the negotiations had resumed, an agreement had not yet been reached.
The governor and legislative leaders were speaking to reporters in Albany.

The New York Times in its Tuesday edition said that the tax extension talks between the state's top Democrat, Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan), and New York City officials had broken down in a dispute over how the funds would be spent.
Silver said he wanted written assurances from Mayor Rudolph Giuliani that he would use a substantial share of the money to hire more police officers.

But Giuliani, a Republican, has said he wants any bill extending the tax to give him more flexibility in spending the money. The 12.5 percent surcharge, which has helped pay for 6,000 new police officers for New York City, is projected to raise $455 million in the city's 1997 fiscal year, and $473 million in the following year.
